utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are no preliminaries announced. Therefore, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time to inform the parties that the Chamber has received the e-mail exchanges between Mr. Simovic and the Defence. The Chamber makes it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Nikolic, yes. If I -- yes, it was Mr. Nikolic. Apologies for mixing them up. The Chamber has looked at it and doesn't see any reason to further pursue the matter, but would like to make the e-mail exchange available to the parties, and if the parties take any different position, then of course we will hear from them, if there is any relevant matter in it. Madam Registrar, you are hereby instructed to make the e-mail exchange as sent through the VWS to make it available to the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Ivetic will now continue his examination. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to take up where we left off with 65 ter number 31002.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could have the second page in the English, the first page in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, on the Serbian your name appears at number 36 in the English, it's four down from the top. And if we go to the entry for the 12th of July, which is 12 squares to the right of your name in the English and is under the column 12 in the Serbian original, we see the notation, "08-BD." What does this notation mean?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This notation means that on that day, on that date, from 0800 hours I was assigned to combat duty. "BD" refers to combat duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does that correspond to when you were activated within the PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I see the notation "BD" for the next eight squares to the right, that brings us to 20 July. And then there is an entry that spans across the remainder of the squares, "SJB," and then it looks like it says "Srebrenica." What would both sets of markings mean?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These notations in the squares refer to combat duty up to -- well, BD, that's combat duty. And then from then on, it's SJB Srebrenica which means that from that time on, I was assigned to Srebrenica police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does this document accurately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we enlarge also the original so that we have a better look at it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have the original on the entire screen and zoom in. That might be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And to what column are you referring, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Under 36, it's the column from 12 to 20, and then from 21 on to 29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have a look at 29 as well? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, does this document accurately depict your duty assignments from the period of 12 July to 20 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This shows my assignments in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where were you the entire period that is marked as BD, combat engagement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, marked as combat duty, I was in the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, perhaps I'm a bit lost but have you paid attention already -- we have BD, several times and then we have one time we have BDSJ. Do we know already what that means? And then the next one is B before it starts with Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had covered that, I believe that is at SJB which would be Stanica Javne Bezbednosti which would be the police station Srebrenica. That's I believe what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's how you understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: SJB. Let me -- I want to enlarge it for myself as well. Could we zoom in on --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 21 and 22 I believe is the column numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where can we find SJB? I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I only see SJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then B is in the next box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: SJB in the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the next box. Yes, indeed, that's what was confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed to explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd like to add anything to your -- we have looked at it now. If you want to add anything to your previous answer, if it's directly related to the questions, you may do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The log-book, the duty log-book, was kept in the Bratunac police station which means that when it says combat duty, I completed combat duty; and then after that, I was in the SJB Srebrenica, in the public security station Srebrenica. That's where I was assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I had tendered this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31002 receives number D585, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, D585 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to 65 ter number 1D03027. Is this 1D03027?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think if you're looking for the other log-book, it's -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What I'm looking for I have up in my e-court -- there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There it is, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision of the Ministry of the Interior, assigning me to the police station in Srebrenica, which is part of the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is this the document that you identified in paragraph 20 of your statement as having a date that came after your actual order to appear in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does this document actually state the date that you commenced duties in Srebrenica police station as a member of that police station rather than the separate duty as a PJP policeman?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This shows that according to this decision, I was appointed a police officer in the Srebrenica public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not hear the date, interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat the date. The interpreters did not hear the date.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 21st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3027 receives number D586, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D586 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would next like to look up 1D3029.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document dated 18 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order issued by the chief of the public security centre, ordering members of the police force who had worked in the public security station in Srebrenica to be activated and to be sent back to the Srebrenica police station to receive their further assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was this order communicated to you in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The other persons listed in this order, is this an accurate listing of persons who with you were assigned as regular policemen of the SJB Srebrenica as of 21 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an accurate list and these are the police officers who used to work in the Srebrenica police station before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And who is the chief of the police station in Srebrenica, your new boss, as of 21 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the Srebrenica public security station at that moment was Petko Pavlovic. He was the acting chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3029 receives number D587, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the Karadzic case were you also shown the original Srebrenica police station log-book by the Prosecution counsel?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the original book was shown to me in the Babovic case from the Srebrenica police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And just to be clear, this original log-book, was that something that you had told the Prosecution about or given to them during your interview in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, I made a mistake. I was thinking about this other document, but the document that you're talking about, yes, I saw it in the Karadzic case and in 2001 I told the investigators about this document, about its location, and in fact where it was archived.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I think I've confused you. Let's call up the document so we can have it in front of us and know which one we are talking about, 1D3028 in e-court. This document, sir, the log-book from Srebrenica station, service roster, this is the one I'm asking about. Is this something that you told the OTP about or gave them during your interview in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was shown to me by the Prosecution here. The Prosecutor showed me this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to being shown this log-book by the Prosecution in the Blagojevic case, when had you last seen it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document in the Srebrenica public security station where I worked, and this document, or rather, the front page, this is what I wrote. This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 of the same in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the names of the persons that are listed here? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recognise some names. I do know those police officers personally. And as for some other names, I don't know them. I don't know these people. But I think that they were all members of the 2nd Company, albeit from other police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, when you say "2nd Company," 2nd Company of what formation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Company of the PJP. There were members of that company who had come from other police stations but they were also engaged in Srebrenica, just as I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now the document -- the page we have up in the e-court right now is dated 12 July 1995. We see your name listed at the bottom in the -- in both versions and it says 19 to 24, sector 1. Does that comport with your recollection as to where you were performing duties on the 12th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was performing this duty. I was in the town of Srebrenica, in the very centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here we should see -- it's on the left-hand side in the B/C/S, and it's the full page in the English, we see the notations for 13 July 1995. And we see your name in approximately the middle of the page. Does this comport to your recollection of the duties that you were performing on 13 of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is where I was on duty service, together with Danilo Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender the document at this time as the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3028 receives number D588, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D588 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, for my last topic I would ask we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you for your answers to my questions today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. McCloskey, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey. You'll find him to your right. Mr. McCloskey is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you first become aware that you were named at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you first become aware that you were named in the Srebrenica events when it was -- when you were named publicly in the Krstic trial? This was in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the first time my name was mentioned pertaining to the events in Srebrenica was in 2001 when I gave a statement to the OTP investigators in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that was in March of 2001, with Jean-Rene Ruez?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you had received a summons as a suspect for your role in the Srebrenica events prior to meeting with Mr. Ruez, had you not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that occasion, when I met with Mr. Ruez, I was interrogated as a suspect, and I can say that he was quite unfair in the course of those interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you had received a summons indicating you were a suspect and mentioning Srebrenica before seeing Mr. Ruez; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the summons did not specify the exact allegations against me. It only stated Srebrenica 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as a result of receiving that summons, you will recall that you told us you went into the Bratunac police station where you were still a Bratunac officer and looked up some records to help refresh your recollection upon your whereabouts during the Srebrenica times; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in order to ascertain some facts, I know where I was, I know about my movements, but I had to verify that in order to have some official documents corroborating those facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as we know now, you knew of this book. This is -- we now have it marked as D58 [sic], the Srebrenica log-book. You knew that that book existed in July 1995 and you knew that it existed in 2001 when you met with Mr. Ruez, did you not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about that book in July 1995. As I've already told you, I actually wrote the words on the front page of that book, the service roster, but I did not know what happened to that book until you showed me that book here at this Tribunal in a previous case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you said the number would be D58.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I thought I said D588. I'm sorry. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, since you were interrupted anyhow, one matter. You said you were unfairly treated during the interview. Mr. McCloskey, may I take it that the interview was conducted in accordance with Rule 43, that is, audio recorded and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have the tape of that interview and it is uploaded in e-court if anyone would like review it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this Chamber always is very seriously concerned about any allegation of misconduct of investigators. If you say you were unfairly treated, please tell us in what way and then we'll verify that on the basis of audio and transcription of your interview. So if you stick to that, that you were unfairly treated, then we'll further explore that. Is that what you wish us to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not necessary to investigate any further. I have the video and audio recording as well, I mean that interview. But my opinion is that it was unfair because there was a bit of voice raising and so on, but there you go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is a rather serious accusation you make. I was treated unfairly. And then to say: Well, you don't have to look into that, comes as a surprise. We also could have a look in it to see whether you're reliable in giving evidence on unfair treatment. We take these matters seriously. If you say: Stay out, okay. We don't have to do it, then we'll further ask the parties whether or not we should. But please be aware that just in the first answer to start saying: I was unfairly treated, may have some follow-up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's been a long time since then. It doesn't really matter that much now but I just sort of said it because I wasn't ready, I didn't have some information and so on and so forth. As I've already said, it's been quite a while and I don't really want to go into that any more. I said what I said and there you go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So as you've said, that you saw this book when I showed it to you back in April of 2004 in the Blagojevic case; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, and I saw it in July when I wrote that and when I had contact with that book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now could we go to D588. And let's go to that page that Mr. Ivetic left on, and that should be page 5 -- excuse me, page 6 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, am I wrong in understanding that the document we just looked at is an excerpt consisting of four pages, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Ours somehow we have got different ones but it's page 4 in both languages. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the page where -- yes, the 13th of July is dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Are the two corresponding? That is my problem now, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can perhaps assist, the questions that Mr. McCloskey asked were relating to the other log-book from the Bratunac Brigade and now we are on the Srebrenica log-book. They are two separate documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have been talking about only one log-book --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- the Srebrenica book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Not if you reference his interview from 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The record is clear. He's wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you consider the record to be clear and you're convinced that your right, Mr. McCloskey, that's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I move for the Chamber to review the interview from 2001 in its entirety to see which document is discussed therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He's correct. The document was discussed in that interview. I did not discuss the document with the witness. The only document I have discussed with the witness is this one, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's D588.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- 588, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we are talking about that, about nothing else at this moment. Is that clear to you as well, Witness? We are talking exclusively about the log-book. You said you put the text on the cover of it in your own handwriting at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record then, Your Honours, then I'm lost by Mr. McCloskey's introduction to these questions at page 12 and 13, talking about the log-book from the Bratunac that he reviewed. So this is where the confusion arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We all get confused, if we could just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We start all over again. Avoid any confusion, Mr. McCloskey, because the Chamber has what was shown to the witness when it should always be perfectly clear. Let's just start over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we all remember when Mr. Ivetic showed you this page with your name on it, 13 July. It says "duty service" and where would that have been, duty service, if you can tell?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty service is at the police station in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We can see we are on 13 July, let's go to the next page. And here we can see, in the English, under the Domavija Hotel, I think we need to get -- I don't -- we see Nenad Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We need the original Serbian. Here we go. And if we could blow that Serbian up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, if I could hand you the original book, so you could look at it and see the actual original. This is still on 13 July, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There is no date here but there is the time when I am working.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the hour you were -- your working hour you referred to a second ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 07 until 1900 hours. That is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And on the next page you can see "14 July" written?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this reference to you is on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just see from 7 until 19. That's the only thing I see here. As for the date, I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, apparently you're very familiar with all these documents so therefore you tell us it's about Hotel Domavija. It doesn't say so. That may well be the case but now you also say the next entry is next date entry is the 14th. Where do we see that? The -- it's not on this page, as far as I can see. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's on the next page, Mr. President, it does say the Hotel Domavija on the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says security of Domavija and Drina, that's what I read on the -- what is on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I added "hotel." That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- no. And the same now for the 14th, where do we find this in this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's a four-page document. That's a bit of a problem. You have chosen an excerpt apparently where the 14th is not covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's a document which was uploaded by the Defence, this excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, well, whatever, you're using it at this moment, and since you have the book in your hands, it means that you could have chosen a selection different, which meets your needs. But perhaps if the Chamber later could have a look -- or is there any dispute about the 14th to be the next date entry, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is no dispute that it's the next date entry in the book. As to what the entries refer to at the hours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. The only question was whether Mr. McCloskey puts to the witness that the next date entry is the 14th, and therefore, that Mr. McCloskey asks him whether the witness agrees that then the entry which we see before us is about the 13th, that's apparently --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that was my point because it's right in front of him and he'll see that and he's just agreed with it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, let's move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- and that leaves us where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And, Mr. McCloskey, on the previous page what would be the date, where his day begins? Can you see that? I mean he can look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, if we go back a page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Three in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Those are the entries up to the next page, the same date as that date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the Prosecution's position, that the next page which is still under the heading of 13 July is on the 13 July and the next page after that says the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So if we could go to in the original the next page and if we could blow up, especially the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, your name and this number. And you can see, sir, next to your name that there has been some alterations in the number, can't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are signs that this has been altered. You asked me that in 2004, but it's not I. I didn't correct this in any way. I didn't change anything. I worked from 7 to 19 together with Obrenovic Darko and on that same day, I was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that is the case in 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last part of your answer, the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 07 until 1900 hours, I worked providing security in Domavija. And that same day, from 1900 hours until 07, I was at the police station of Srebrenica where I was on duty service. And the duty service is the first one that is recorded and then the other services follow only after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you see as you look in the original that prior to the alteration, it would have been noted 1900 to 0900, but that was written over? The 1 was written over with a 0. You can see that; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that there were some corrections, and I cannot confirm any of that. I never made these alterations. I don't know who did that and I don't know --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness again spoke off mike. We did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you come closer to the microphone and repeat the last part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be seen that some alterations or corrections were made as far as this time is concerned, next to my name; however, I don't understand. I did not did this. I don't know who could have done this and I don't know why this was done, as far as these corrections are concerned. And as the Prosecutor also says, there are some numbers here and he can discern them as for the prefer ones too. I mean, I cannot establish any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you were aware, when Mr. Ruez spoke to you and thereafter, that the events that you were a suspect for took place during the day on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was told there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So the original -- what appears to be, in the Prosecution's view, the original 1900 to 0900 would have left you free on that day with no alibi?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I know who wrote this? The Office of the Prosecutor could have written this too, if somebody is wanting to do something to someone. How can we establish anything now in relation to these alterations? We have to be realistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there is no need to comment on that. Witness, I think it is appropriate for me at this moment, in view of the line of questioning, that I inform you that if any truthful answer to any question that is put to you would entail a risk of incriminating yourself, that I put to you the content of Rule 90(E) and I read it for you. "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." Now, let it be clear that if you consider that a truthful answer might tend to incriminate you, that you can address me and that you ask to be relieved from answering that question, which the Chamber will then further consider. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, as we did many years ago in Blagojevic, I think you'll note that there are other alterations in this book, aren't there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. That is what we established. Lawyer Karnavas was there, and also -- I mean in these further lists there were these corrections, alterations, whatever. I don't know. Not only by my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But the only alteration on your name for 13 July is right in front of you; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the 13th of July, that's what it says, but last time we also established that there were other alterations on other pages, in connection with other members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I agree, and that's all for this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I see it's break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there a possibility that the Chamber would have a look at the original after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We take a break, Mr. Deronjic, and we would like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to come in, perhaps the Chamber could have a look at the book which it prefers to look at in court. The usher has now left -- oh, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, we put a little yellow tab for that area mentioning the 13th and 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Concerned that we couldn't find page 3 or 4, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Always trying to be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed. We could give it back for the time being. We may want to consult it at a later stage again, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for my next and I hope last topic, could we start off with the map book P01087, page 10 in e-court, to help orient us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But as we are waiting for that, there will be a map graphic that will come up in a minute, but how many years now have you been a professionally trained police officer?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started working in the police in 1987, so actively this is 27 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you prepare reports that go into files and dossiers for courtroom and judicial processes?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could flip that map around. Thank you. And this is a to-scale map graphic, and I'm sure if you take a look at it you'll recognise these areas. And I want to ask you about the intersection of the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road and the -- what's called the Milici-Zvornik road. That intersection at Konjevic Polje, from there to Bratunac is, what, about 10 kilometres -- or excuse me, about 20 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, 21 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And from Bratunac to Srebrenica is about 10 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And going to July 1995, the check-point you've talked about is at that intersection at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the check-point in Konjevic Polje that was held by the Bratunac police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as I think you've clarified, one of the PJP units, the 6th Company of the PJP which is made up of older -- older folks actually had a -- in July 1995, they were stationed there along with some regular police officers like yourself; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And one of those members of the 6th PJP was Dragisa Zekic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, and I know Dragisa Zekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Mirko Peric, was he there also as a member of the 6th PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mirko Peric. Now, I don't know whether he was in the 6th Company but that can be checked. No problem whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was he a police officer back then?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that during the war, he became active as a policeman. He had not worked as a policeman before the war. He worked in the field of catering.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Had he been a waiter at the Hotel Fontana before the war?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And before the war, did you know a policeman named -- a Muslim man named Resid Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard the name, but I didn't know him personally. But I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Had you heard from Dragisa Zekic that Resid Sinanovic had actually been held at that check-point during the period that the Muslims were going through that area in July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that I heard the name, but I heard another name too, a name that you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did you or did you actually hear from Dragisa Zekic that Resid Sinanovic had been at that check-point during those days?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I hadn't heard that. I heard that he had seen him but where he saw him and what happened to this Resid Sinanovic, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So had you heard that Dragisa Zekic had seen Resid Sinanovic while he was on duty?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from Dragisa Zekic, that he had seen that person, Resid Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was that during the time frame that Muslims were moving in a column from Srebrenica up through the woods towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when that happened. That's a question for Dragisa Zekic, not for me. I mean, I cannot give any comments regarding what Dragisa Zekic saw, who he saw, who he talked to, what he did. I wouldn't want to give any comments on that because I was not there and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I stop you there. You were asked whether you learned from Dragisa Zekic that he had seen Resid Sinanovic while he was on duty. Did he tell you anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just told me that he had seen him. I'm sorry, may I? Now I'm supposed to carry out some kind of investigation to ask him what? I mean nothing. That's the only thing I heard from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're only invited to answer the questions, and do I understand your testimony to be that Dragisa Zekic told you, "I saw Sinanovic" without saying where, when, what circumstances, he just said, "I saw him." That's how I understand your testimony and that is you're confirming that by nodding "yes" apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Zekic would have seen him after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And before the war ended?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But was that time-period in the days after Srebrenica fell when the Muslims were going from Srebrenica through the woods, Konjevic Polje, to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about this? I mean, I take it that you want to guide the witness in a certain direction, but there is no --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think the witness has already answered this a couple of lines above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could I get an answer? This is an important point to try to identify the time-frame by where Dragisa Zekic saw Resid Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the question consists of two issues. Would he have seen him in the days after Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was answered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we got an answer for that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the other question then would be when the Muslims were going from Srebrenica through the woods, Konjevic Polje to Zvornik, and my question was whether there is any dispute about that. Is there any dispute about that, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That fact itself, no, I can't imagine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Then phrase the question in such a way that we get -- we know better because that's what the question says now. But is it awareness of the witness? Is that -- of that happening? Is that -- please rephrase the second part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there -- are you aware of the time-period after Srebrenica fell that Muslims were moving from Srebrenica, Muslim able-bodied men, and others were moving from Srebrenica through the woods past Konjevic Polje up towards Zvornik and on to Nezuk or that general area?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know. It's general knowledge that they were heading down that route towards the area that was to become Federation at one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So was it during this time-frame of this Muslim movement that Resid Sinanovic told you he -- sorry, that Dragisa Zekic told you he saw Resid Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was in that period that Dragisa told me that, that he had seen Sinanovic, Resid Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And now in your statement -- I want to go to that time period on the morning of 12 July, you say that you got off duty at 8.00 a.m. And then on paragraph 15 of your statement, which is now D584, should be page 4 on both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should not be broadcast; it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And it says: "After that, i.e., after 1500 hours on 12 July 1995, we members of the 2nd Company from the police station in Bratunac went to Srebrenica. I do not know how many of us there were, but I believe that we managed to fit into two buses together with some other policemen from the Zvornik centre. Slavoljub Mladjenvic, my commander, i.e., the commander of the 2nd Company, of the Special Police unit, was also with us." And you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, if I may clarify this issue, I can be actually grateful to you for asking me this question because you have found a document indicating that the entire 2nd Company of the PJP was not in Srebrenica which is precisely what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not arguing with Mr. McCloskey. The question was put to you whether you stand by this testimony in paragraph 15. Do you or do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the question be put to me again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The portion was read to you and the question is whether you stand by that evidence in your statement or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statement that's right in front of me on the screen; is that the one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 15. If you want to re-read it, you can read it from the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I stand by what is written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then wait for the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how many platoons did the 2nd PJP Company have at this time-period?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know, but it can be checked. It's not a problem, the number of platoons in it the 2nd Company because I was not in charge of the 2nd Company. I was merely one of the members of that company. I was not even a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So does the number 2 sound correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't tell you, but it's not a problem. It can be checked. You can determine the number of platoons. I don't know how many platoons there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in a platoon during that time, that would be roughly between 40 and 60 men?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The only thing I do know is that officers from all police stations were in that company, four to five people from each police station per company. So now you can figure out how many people there were in a company and how many people there were in a platoon and how many platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you're an experienced, trained police officer. You have been a suspect for your involvement at the 2nd PJP in July 1995 and after all these years, you can't tell us, is that -- you want me to figure it out? You can't tell us how many platoons were in the 2nd PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just tell you one more thing, sir. I did not serve in the military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please answer the question. Mr. McCloskey asked you whether it's true that you can't tell him now how many platoons were there in the 2nd PJP and he gave you a few reasons why he thought that you would be in a position to tell him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the record at line 8 the witness answered the question, and so now he's being asked to explain, he started to explain, and you interrupted had him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I urged him to answer the question which was put again to him, Mr. Ivetic. If your objection was question asked question answered, then you could have raised that objection. I just urged him to respond. Please proceed, Mr. -- but could we receive an answer to the question again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already answered. I don't know how many platoons there were, how many people there were in a company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can now go to some of your Blagojevic testimony, it should be at 65 ter 1D2236 beginning page 34 in e-court. And, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just a caution, this is the full copy with private and public, just to make sure that we are paying attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you'll read the relevant portions to the witness so that it doesn't have to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed and take care that nothing appears on the screen or is read which is from private or closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So on 12 July in the afternoon, did you become aware that there was combat between the Muslims from Srebrenica and Serb forces in the area just outside Srebrenica, Konjevic Polje area?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me if I became aware?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, of the combat between the Muslims and the Serb forces from the Muslim breakout on 12 July, when you were being sent to Srebrenica, according to your version.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's at page 34, I'll read you the relevant part. And this is in the context of you being sent down with your group to Srebrenica, and I asked you: "Q. Was there any part of the 2nd Company that was sent somewhere else?" Your answer is: "A. I don't know about that but I don't think so. I don't think anybody was sent somewhere else. "Q. Well, on this -- on the afternoon, evening hours of 12 July, Muslims from Srebrenica, armed Muslims, were breaking through the area around Konjevic Polje than was a combat zone. Were you aware of that?" Your answer: "A. Yes. "Q. So you, you're aware that Konjevic Polje has become a combat zone shortly after the time that you left it, so you must have been relieved to have been able to get an assignment to go to Srebrenica which was not a combat zone." Your answer is: "A. You could put it that way. "Q. And were any of your colleagues so unlucky that they got assigned to go to the combat zone, Konjevic Polje, Ravni Buljim, Cerska?" Your answer: "A. I don't know about that. I know that they were at Konjevic Polje, that's where the 6th Company was. Now, as to the rest, to the other areas, I don't know if anybody went. "Q. Well" -- Here's my question: "Well, I'm talking about the 2nd Company, your crew. You would have known if they had been in combat if some of them would have gotten sent to combat, wouldn't you?" Your answer on the next page: "A. No, no. Those of us who went up there, they didn't send us to any other places except to the area around the town of Srebrenica." So let me just break this down and ask you a question or two. My question on line 9: "Well, on the afternoon, evening hours of the 12th of July, Muslims of Srebrenica, armed Muslims, were breaking through the area around Konjevic Polje and that was a combat zone were you aware of that?" In Blagojevic you said yes, you were aware of that. I just asked you a similar question and you said you were not aware of that at that time. Which is it? Were you or were you not, on the 12th of July, aware of combat going on in the areas I talk about here?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. You seem to be unable to understand me. I simply don't understand. I kept saying and I keep saying now in all those situations I was just an ordinary police officer, nobody asked me anything, and I was not in charge of anything. I was not supposed to know things so why was I supposed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not arguing. Mr. McCloskey put to you that in the other case you gave an answer which he considers to be different from the answer you give now. You don't have to defend or to emphasise why your present answer is the better one or the -- you were asked why you give a different answer today compared to that other day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm telling you, things were not clear to me because I kept saying that I was just an ordinary police officer, I had nothing to do with it, and now why I said that, I suppose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I establish that you want to give us your explanation rather than to answer the question. Next question, please, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's go to Exhibit P2111. So as we can see, that this is a report from the Zvornik CJB, the public security centre. That's the security centre that had overall dealings with the various PJP units, that they basically came from that security centre; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And there was a -- a 1st PJP unit, as well as a 2nd and a 6th, as we've already talked about; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that unit had also members from Bratunac, people that you would have known?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the 1st Company?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. I knew them. I knew them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that was -- was that unit a bit fitter or a bit more combat-ready than the 2nd?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I want to direct your attention -- this is a dispatch on 12 July, and we know it's after 10.30 from just the information in the first couple of pages but it's not clear exactly when it was sent out, aside from that. And it's in the name of -- well it's the chief of the S -- CJB and that at the time was Dragomir Vasic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Dragomir Vasic was the chief of the Zvornik CJB, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I want to draw your attention to paragraph 5. It's going to be page 2 in the B/C/S and part of it in the English but let's go over the English first. And at page -- at paragraph 5 it says: "Acting upon President Karadzic's order which was conveyed to us today over the phone, the 2nd PJ -- the 2nd Company of the Zvornik PJP [two platoons, 60 men] shall be dispatched to Srebrenica with a task to secure all facilities of vital importance in the town, at all the costs and protect them from looting and misappropriation." That's what you've been talking about, your group going to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "It will carry out the task without the co-operation of the military police which is busy with other tasks, a platoon of this company will lie in ambush at Ravni Buljim since the Muslim groups were spotted fleeing along the axis." So here we see an assignment or an intention to send a platoon of the 2nd PJP to Ravni Buljim. Tell us roughly, is Ravni Buljim between Jaglici and Konjevic Polje in a very rugged area?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It's a mountainous area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So were you in the group of the 2nd PJP that was assigned to that area on the 12 July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told you where I was, and I am not aware of any group being assigned to this task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were not asked whether you were aware of any group. The question was whether you were in the group of the 2nd PJP that was assigned to that area on the 12th of July. I do understand your answer to be that you were not. By the way, the answer of the witness of course is caused by a composite question, certain -- various elements contained in it. Mr. McCloskey, that's what causes it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, so your answer was that you weren't even aware that a platoon of your group which we just saw was sent to Srebrenica, you weren't even aware that your colleagues went off to combat while you went to look after Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit 65 ter 5884 -- excuse me, 65 ter 5881. And let's go to the next page in both languages. And directing our attention to the bottom of the page under "other business", we see that on the first page, that this was a bulletin from the Zvornik public security centre. Under "other business," it says, and we also note that this is for the period of 13 and 14 July: "Due to infiltration of enemy military formations from Srebrenica into the zone of the Zvornik CJB and areas of Konjevic Polje, Cerska, Han Pogled, which have in common Snagovo, Maricici, and other places at risk, the 1st, 2nd, 5th, and 6th Companies of the Zvornik CJB are engaged." Were you engaged in this -- the area around Konjevic Polje or Cerska on 13 or 14 July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would offer this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 05881 receives number P6686, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6686 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware that members of the 2nd PJP -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just correct myself? Document 5881 should receive number P8867, Your Honours, not -- P6687 instead of P6686. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm now a bit confused. It therefore should receive P8 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 5881 should receive number P6687 instead of P6686, as previously stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. P6687 is now admitted, and P6686 remains the same as it was when it was admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time that parts of your unit were in these areas as described in this document, involved in the combat blocking?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Ivetic any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. McCloskey, at transcript page 12 and 13 today asked you if you looked up some records in the police station before going to the interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in March of 2001. Could you please explain for us how it is that you went to look up these records? Were you alone?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to look at these records, the assistant commander -- the deputy commander, was with me, the one who had written up these records. So it was in his presence that I had a look at these records.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say "records," could you be more precise as to what records you were looking up together with the assistant commander or deputy commander prior to going to the interview with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was looking at records that had to do with service assignments recorded in the police station of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so that we are clear - if we can call up D585 in e-court - is this the document, sir, that you looked up with the assistant commander in the Bratunac police station to refresh your recollection prior to going to the interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the document that I had a look at before going to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you've thus far referred to him as the assistant or deputy commander. Could you please give us the name of the individual who -- in whose presence you examined this record at the police station in Bratunac in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Nedeljkovic was the name of that man, and he works at the Bratunac police station to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At that time, in 2001, when you went to look at this record, where was the original of this record being kept, at what location?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original was kept in the safe of the Bratunac police station, and I think that that is where it is to this day, the original book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time that you looked at it with Mr. Nedeljkovic, were any modifications made to it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no corrections were made. It was in the original, as it had been before, so there were no corrections made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were there any other documents or records at the Bratunac police station that you reviewed prior to going to the interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in Banja Luka in March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to look at other documentation, except for this service roster or, rather, the log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you try to find other documentation that you believed existed that covered this time-period that would have been kept in the Bratunac police station?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't try anything else in relation to this documentation except for this documentation that I found and reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to switch gears and I'd like to talk about the Srebrenica police station log-book and so that we are on the same page, if we can call up D588 in e-court. Now that we have this document up on the screen, sir, I'd like to ask you, focusing on this document, from the Srebrenica police station, was this a document that you had occasion to locate and review prior to going for an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in Banja Luka in March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have the opportunity to see this document before. Actually, I saw it when I wrote that, but before going to Banja Luka, I did not have an opportunity to see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You just said you saw it when you wrote that. Are you referring to the text that is now on the screen which would be the cover of the log-book?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. What is written here on the cover is what I had written. This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I note it also has Nenad at the bottom of the -- of the selection. When was this written on the cover of the log-book?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was written when that first text was written, that is to say on the 12th of July, and this, what you can see down here, is my abbreviated signature, D. Nenad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you be more specific? You said the 12th of July. What year?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were you charged with keeping the log-book of the SJB Srebrenica or was somebody else in charge of keeping the log-book of the SJB Srebrenica from 12th July 1995 onwards?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not charged with keeping the log-book. I just made this initial record. As for the rest of the lists, this was done by the then-deputy commander, that is to say, another policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the second page in both versions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could the witness also give the name of that other policeman, the then-deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Milisav Gavric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And until when was he the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly but I know that he was appointed deputy commander in that period, but I don't know until when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it for a year that he stayed there or for five years or for one month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Longer than a month, but I cannot tell you exactly. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking for an exact answer but more than a month. Could it be three months? I mean, you worked there, wasn't it -- weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. But that can be confirmed through other checks. I mean, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I cannot confirm anything by other checks. Was it well, let's say, until the end of the war that he was there, or until after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. He was. While I was up there, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so he remained in that position until the end of the war or longer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up until the end of the war. I know that I left Srebrenica in 1996. I went to the border and he was there carrying out those duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, looking at the B/C/S original of page 2 of this document that's dated the 12th of July, 1995, are any of these entries your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not a single thing here was written by me. This is not my handwriting. It was not written in my own hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During your examination by Mr. McCloskey, you kept referring to other entries that had been altered and I'd like to ask you to look at the second half of the page in relation to Novicic, Jovanovic, Djuric, and Ilic. Is that one of the other alterations that you and Mr. McCloskey went through during the Blagojevic trial in relation to the original of this book?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. There are some alterations here, with these other numbers, Novicic, Jovanovic, Djuric, and Ilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put just one question, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, whose handwriting is that on the left side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the handwriting to the best of my knowledge, as far as I can remember, of Milisav Gavric, the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And was he responsible for all entries in the entire log-book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, the list of policemen, the activities of the service, and working hours, from when until when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was only this man who made the entries; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where was this service log-book of the Srebrenica police station kept, according to your knowledge and information?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's vague. If we could have a time-frame, that would have meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, were you referring to the time when it was produced or are you referring to any later time?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The period of 1995, where was it kept during that time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was kept at the Srebrenica police station or, rather, in the office of the duty service.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like for you to look at the entry that has been changed on this page, there is a 7 that looks like it's been written over an 8. And now I'd like to then turn to the next page in the B/C/S and the English, and if we could flip the B/C/S to focus -- pardon me, it's going to be -- pardon me, it's going to be the -- it's going to be I think the fourth page in the B/C/S and if you look at the 7 that has been written in next to your name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does that 7 appear to be in the same style as the 7 we just looked at on page 2?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that it's the same style of writing the number 7 on this page, like on the previous ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 4 now, in both versions -- or I apologise, the next page. I apologise, the next page. I think it's 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You uploaded a four-page document, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then it was page 4. I apologise for having the pages jumbled up. Is this then page 4? Or -- ah, okay, this is page 4. I guess the other page doesn't -- is not uploaded. I apologise, the prior page, then, it's the prior page I'm looking for, the right-hand side of the same. If we can zoom in on the right-hand side of that page in the original B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do there also appear to be alterations in the bottom right-hand corner to the Serbian word "opstine"?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, over here certain alterations and changes can be seen, done in pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the summons that you received to appear for an interview for the Office of the Prosecutor, it did not list any precise incident or any date or time of any incident that you were being questioned on, did it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to the actual meeting that you had with Mr. Ruez of the Office of the Prosecutor in Banja Luka in March of 2001, did you know the time or the facts of the incident about which they were interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not made aware of any of this through the summons, I mean in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And from the 12th through the 20th of July, 1995, when you were in Srebrenica town, as part of the 2nd Company of the PJP, when you were not on duty, where would you and other PJP members be situated and what would you be doing?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were not on duty, we were getting some rest. We slept at the police station of Srebrenica, and also in this building above the police station in Srebrenica, in the so-called miners' buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to -- focus on the left-hand side of the B/C/S, and if we can go to the prior page -- we have it on the screen already in English. It says, in the heading of the part where you are identified, it says, in Serbian "sluzba dezurna," in English "duty service." Could you explain for us what that particular assignment means?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty service means duty service in the Bratunac police station, contacts with patrols, sending patrols to services, giving orders if any, and all the other things that a duty policeman does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have been recorded in the transcript as saying duty service in the Bratunac police station. Is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is at the police station in Srebrenica, the duty service there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, are we at the time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are. We are even already beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's my duty to keep an eye on that, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is there any way we can finish up right now or in the next few minutes? I apologise. I just -- there is a very important issue that I have outside of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could extend another five minutes I think we can finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that is -- I see Mr. Mladic is nodding in agreement. Then we'll gladly accommodate you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to page -- to the next page in both languages, now, the heading at the top of the page talks about Domavija and Drina. Where were these locations vis-à-vis the police station in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Domavija is a hotel in Srebrenica. It is some 300 metres away from the police station in Srebrenica on the left-hand side, that is to say when we are facing Jadar. And Drina is a forestry facility right next door to Domavija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps a very short question, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was specifically there which needed security?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, nothing. I'm telling you, that's where the main office of the Drina forestry company was and there was the Domavija Hotel as well. There was no one at the hotel but security had to be provided for that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You sent a full-time security to a building where there is just nothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a team. It's two or three policemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
